title: Educational Measurement and Evaluation
topics: Educational objectives and domains of learning
Meaning and scope of measurement and evaluation

items.q: Which of the following best describes Z score?
o: the accuracy with which scores forecast a learner's later performance
a transformation that states the distance of a raw score from the mean in deviation units
the extent to which a question separates the high scorers from the low scorers
the gathering and interpretation of information about a learner for the purpose of decision making
items.s: Z score: a transformation that states the distance of a raw score from the mean in deviation units. The other options describe Discrimination index, Assessment, Predictive validity.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Moderation of marks.
o: the adjustment of scores from different markers so that they can be compared
a transformation that states the distance of a raw score from the mean in deviation units
the accuracy with which scores forecast a learner's later performance
the extent to which a question separates the high scorers from the low scorers
items.s: Moderation of marks: the adjustment of scores from different markers so that they can be compared. The other options describe Z score, Discrimination index, Predictive validity.

items.q: Which term is described by “the putting together of separate parts into a whole that was not there before”?
o: Psychomotor domain
Cognitive domain
Synthesis
Educational objective
items.s: Synthesis is the putting together of separate parts into a whole that was not there before.
items.t: Educational objectives and domains of learning

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Interest inventory?
o: the consistency of an instrument in giving similar results when it is used again
the class of learning outcomes that concern interest, attitude and value
a list of activities to which a respondent reacts in order to reveal vocational liking
the steady accumulation of scores from class work, tests and projects over a period
items.s: Interest inventory: a list of activities to which a respondent reacts in order to reveal vocational liking. The other options describe Continuous assessment, Affective domain, Reliability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Psychomotor domain.
o: the share of the total mark that is allotted to one component of assessment
the average distance of scores from the mean of their distribution
the class of learning outcomes that concern bodily skill and coordination
a paper that measures the gain a learner has made from a course of study
items.s: Psychomotor domain: the class of learning outcomes that concern bodily skill and coordination. The other options describe Achievement test, Weighting, Standard deviation.
items.t: Educational objectives and domains of learning

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Essay item.
o: the class of learning outcomes that concern bodily skill and coordination
the proportion of candidates in the group who answered a question correctly
a question that requires the candidate to organise and write a long answer in prose
the percentage of candidates whose scores fall at or below a particular score
items.s: Essay item: a question that requires the candidate to organise and write a long answer in prose. The other options describe Difficulty index, Psychomotor domain, Percentile rank.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Behavioural objective?
o: the use of a learned rule in a situation that was not met during instruction
a statement with a blank that the candidate supplies with the missing word
the degree to which all the questions of a paper measure one trait
a goal expressed in observable action, with the condition and the standard of performance
items.s: Behavioural objective: a goal expressed in observable action, with the condition and the standard of performance. The other options describe Completion item, Application, Internal consistency.
items.t: Educational objectives and domains of learning

items.q: The statement “the degree to which all the questions of a paper measure one trait” describes which of the following?
o: Test-retest method
Standard error of measurement
Internal consistency
Parallel forms
items.s: Internal consistency is the degree to which all the questions of a paper measure one trait.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Standard score?
o: the use of letter or number symbols to stand for a level of achievement
a score stated in units of standard deviation from the mean of its group
the extent to which a distribution gathers on one side of its centre
the assignment of numerals to the attributes of persons or things according to stated rules
items.s: Standard score: a score stated in units of standard deviation from the mean of its group. The other options describe Measurement, Grading, Skewness.

items.q: Comprehension may be defined as
o: the level of understanding at which a learner restates or explains material in own words
a transformation with a mean of fifty and a standard deviation of ten
a question that asks candidates to pair entries in one list with entries in another
the asking of pupils whom they would choose as companions, used to chart social ties
items.s: Comprehension: the level of understanding at which a learner restates or explains material in own words. The other options describe Matching item, Sociometric technique, T score.
items.t: Educational objectives and domains of learning

items.q: All of the following belong to Item analysis EXCEPT
o: Face validity
Item analysis
Discrimination index
Difficulty index
items.s: Every other option belongs to Item analysis. “Face validity” belongs to Validity of instruments, not Item analysis.

items.q: Which term is described by “a question with one fixed correct response that can be marked without judgement”?
o: Objective item
Distractor
Test
Stem
items.s: Objective item is a question with one fixed correct response that can be marked without judgement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Questionnaire.
o: a written set of questions that respondents complete without the presence of the inquirer
the extent to which a distribution gathers on one side of its centre
the rewriting of a faulty question after its statistics have been examined
the average performance of a reference group used as a standard for judging individuals
items.s: Questionnaire: a written set of questions that respondents complete without the presence of the inquirer. The other options describe Skewness, Norm, Item revision.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Test-retest method?
o: a transformation that states the distance of a raw score from the mean in deviation units
the estimation of consistency by giving the same paper twice to one group
a paper that predicts how well a person will profit from future training
a transformation with a mean of fifty and a standard deviation of ten
items.s: Test-retest method: the estimation of consistency by giving the same paper twice to one group. The other options describe Z score, T score, Aptitude test.

items.q: The statement “the consistency of an instrument in giving similar results when it is used again” describes which of the following?
o: Reliability
Test-retest method
Test length
Internal consistency
items.s: Reliability is the consistency of an instrument in giving similar results when it is used again.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Summative evaluation?
o: the judgement made at the close of a course to certify attainment or decide promotion
a question that asks candidates to pair entries in one list with entries in another
the share of the total mark that is allotted to one component of assessment
a transformation that states the distance of a raw score from the mean in deviation units
items.s: Summative evaluation: the judgement made at the close of a course to certify attainment or decide promotion. The other options describe Matching item, Z score, Weighting.
items.t: Meaning and scope of measurement and evaluation

items.q: The statement “the closeness of the marks that two or more scorers give to the same scripts” describes which of the following?
o: Test length
Inter-rater agreement
Internal consistency
Parallel forms
items.s: Inter-rater agreement is the closeness of the marks that two or more scorers give to the same scripts.

items.q: Median may be defined as
o: the adjustment of scores from different markers so that they can be compared
the steady accumulation of scores from class work, tests and projects over a period
the statement of the change in behaviour that instruction is meant to produce
the middle score when a distribution is arranged in order of size
items.s: Median: the middle score when a distribution is arranged in order of size. The other options describe Educational objective, Continuous assessment, Moderation of marks.

items.q: The statement “a transformation with a mean of fifty and a standard deviation of ten” describes which of the following?
o: Norm-referenced interpretation
Stanine
Z score
T score
items.s: T score is a transformation with a mean of fifty and a standard deviation of ten.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Criterion-referenced interpretation?
o: the judgement made while teaching is still going on in order to improve it
the reading of a score against a fixed standard of what should be known
the middle score when a distribution is arranged in order of size
the trial of a new paper on a small group to remove faults before general use
items.s: Criterion-referenced interpretation: the reading of a score against a fixed standard of what should be known. The other options describe Formative evaluation, Median, Pilot testing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Standard deviation.
o: the average distance of scores from the mean of their distribution
the level of understanding at which a learner restates or explains material in own words
the accuracy with which scores forecast a learner's later performance
the degree to which a paper samples the syllabus it is supposed to cover
items.s: Standard deviation: the average distance of scores from the mean of their distribution. The other options describe Predictive validity, Comprehension, Content validity.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Application.
o: the gap between the highest and the lowest score in a distribution
the use of a learned rule in a situation that was not met during instruction
the file that keeps a pupil's scores and details throughout the school years
the degree to which a paper samples the syllabus it is supposed to cover
items.s: Application: the use of a learned rule in a situation that was not met during instruction. The other options describe Content validity, Range, Cumulative record card.
items.t: Educational objectives and domains of learning

items.q: Standard error of measurement may be defined as
o: the band of doubt within which a candidate's true score probably lies
the use of a learned rule in a situation that was not met during instruction
an index between minus one and plus one showing the strength of a linear relationship
a transformation with a mean of fifty and a standard deviation of ten
items.s: Standard error of measurement: the band of doubt within which a candidate's true score probably lies. The other options describe Product moment correlation, Application, T score.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Construct validity?
o: a form on which an observer records the behaviours noticed during a lesson
a question that requires the candidate to organise and write a long answer in prose
the extent to which scores behave as the theory of the trait says they should
the score that occurs most frequently in a distribution
items.s: Construct validity: the extent to which scores behave as the theory of the trait says they should. The other options describe Essay item, Observation schedule, Mode.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Raw score?
o: the systematic process of judging the worth of achievement or of a programme against stated aims
the marks or number correct obtained before any conversion is made
the count of how many candidates in each score band chose each wrong option
the overall judgement of a pupil's standing built up from several sources of information
items.s: Raw score: the marks or number correct obtained before any conversion is made. The other options describe Evaluation, Appraisal, Distractor analysis.

items.q: The statement “the average distance of scores from the mean of their distribution” describes which of the following?
o: Range
Standard deviation
Mode
Skewness
items.s: Standard deviation is the average distance of scores from the mean of their distribution.

items.q: Report card may be defined as
o: the sheet issued to parents showing a pupil's attainment for the term
a question followed by several suggested answers from which one is to be chosen
the estimation of consistency by giving the same paper twice to one group
a transformation that states the distance of a raw score from the mean in deviation units
items.s: Report card: the sheet issued to parents showing a pupil's attainment for the term. The other options describe Multiple choice item, Test-retest method, Z score.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Test blueprint.
o: a transformation that states the distance of a raw score from the mean in deviation units
the extent to which scores behave as the theory of the trait says they should
the quantification of school traits such as achievement, aptitude, interest and attitude
the grid showing topics, cognitive levels and the number of questions allotted to each

Completion item
Matching item
Stem

Negative discrimination
Difficulty index
Distractor analysis

the consistency of an instrument in giving similar results when it is used again
the asking of pupils whom they would choose as companions, used to chart social ties

Pilot testing

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Difficulty index.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Difficulty index?

a paper that measures the gain a learner has made from a course of study
a question that requires the candidate to organise and write a long answer in prose
the closeness of the marks that two or more scorers give to the same scripts

Difficulty index
Item revision

the marks or number correct obtained before any conversion is made
a paper that measures the gain a learner has made from a course of study

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Criterion validity?

a fault in which weaker candidates answer a question correctly more often than stronger ones
two versions of an instrument built to the same plan but with different questions
a score stated in units of standard deviation from the mean of its group
items.s: Criterion validity: the agreement between scores on an instrument and an outside standard of performance. The other options describe Negative discrimination, Standard score, Parallel forms.

the asking of pupils whom they would choose as companions, used to chart social ties
a nine point scale that reports attainment in broad bands

a response format with five points running from strong agreement to strong disagreement
the putting together of separate parts into a whole that was not there before
a question that asks candidates to pair entries in one list with entries in another
